input_signals.name: Cash-Burn Debt Dependence
input_signals.hypothesis: Net debt issuance predicts lower returns when firms have persistent negative operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: Repeated cash burn makes net borrowing more likely to reflect liquidity pressure than productive financing. The distress condition separates this interpretation from debt issuance by healthy firms funding investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ), indicator( neg( ma( ratio( oancf, at ), 3 ) ), 0 ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Conversion Equity Dependence
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net equity issuance predicts lower returns when reported income is not supported by operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: A large income-to-cash-flow gap identifies latent liquidity pressure or aggressive accruals rather than simply classifying firms as unprofitable. Equity issuance in that state can reveal opportunistic market timing or dependence on outside capital before the underlying cash weakness becomes fully priced.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( ib, oancf ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cash-Backed Distress Deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, dltis), at)), MIN(RANK(RATIO(oancf, at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(re, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Net debt retirement predicts higher returns when a firm with accumulated losses has restored operating cash generation.
input_signals.reasoning: Negative retained earnings identify legacy distress, while positive operating cash flow distinguishes a genuine turnaround from repayment funded through asset liquidation or refinancing. Requiring strong ranks in repayment, cash generation, and legacy distress targets credible balance-sheet repair without restricting the signal to the negative-book-equity tail.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ), min( rank( ratio( oancf, at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Recovery-Funded Net Repayment
input_signals.hypothesis: Net debt repayment predicts higher returns when operating cash flow is improving.
input_signals.reasoning: Improving cash flow makes repayment more likely to represent a sustainable turnaround than asset liquidation or loss of credit access. Using cash-flow change rather than its level reduces exposure to the generic profitability premium and avoids the dispersion compression of the prior three-way distress conjunction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( sub( dltr, dltis ), at ) ), rank( delta( ratio( oancf, at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Liquidity-Funded Debt Repair
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1))), SUB(RANK(RATIO(dltr, ADD(dltr, dltis))), RANK(RATIO(dltis, ADD(dltr, dltis)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: During cash-reserve drawdowns, repayment-dominant debt activity predicts higher returns than issuance-dominant activity.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether firms use liquidity to reduce debt overhang rather than replenish cash while adding debt, a financing-allocation mechanism unrelated to sales growth. The debt-transaction shares restrict the comparison to active borrowers and create interpretable repayment and issuance poles under the same liquidity shock.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( neg( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ) ), sub( rank( ratio( dltr, add( dltr, dltis ) ) ), rank( ratio( dltis, add( dltr, dltis ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dual-Market Distress Funding
input_signals.hypothesis: Simultaneously raising substantial debt and equity predicts lower returns when operating cash flow is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: Tapping both capital markets while internal cash generation is poor indicates unusually broad external-financing dependence, potential debt-market limits, and severe dilution risk. The matched gross-financing amount identifies dual-market funding rather than repackaging either the debt-repayment turnaround or debt-demand mismatch signals.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( min( dltis, sstk ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Externally Funded Distress Payout
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(MIN(ADD(dvc, prstkc), ADD(dltis, sstk)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(oancf, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Simultaneously raising external capital and distributing cash to shareholders predicts lower returns when operating cash flow is weak.
input_signals.reasoning: The matched amount of payouts and external financing identifies financing churn in which distressed firms raise capital while leaking cash to shareholders. This agency and liquidity mechanism differs from dual debt-and-equity dependence because it focuses on the use of proceeds rather than the breadth of funding sources.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( min( add( dvc, prstkc ), add( dltis, sstk ) ), at ) ), rank( neg( ratio( oancf, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Tax-Exhausted Debt Issuance
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(pi, at)), NEG(RATIO(txt, at)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term debt issuance predicts lower returns when pretax income and current tax payments indicate little capacity to use the debt tax shield.
input_signals.reasoning: Debt issued without taxable earnings is less likely to reflect optimal tax financing and more likely to fund losses or refinance obligations. This replaces the repeatedly unsuccessful issuance-extremeness and liquidity-gap combination with a distinct tax-capacity mechanism using a continuous distress state.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), rank( sumrank( neg( ratio( pi, at ) ), neg( ratio( txt, at ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating Cash Debt-Service Coverage
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms repaying debt, stronger operating cash flow relative to repayment obligations predicts higher returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This uses a conventional flow-to-flow coverage ratio and therefore avoids mixing the cash stock with annual financing flows. It also aligns the favorable debt-repayment effect with repayment capacity: low scores identify debt service unsupported by operations, while high scores identify sustainable deleveraging.
input_signals.author: proposer

input_signals.name: External Payout Funding Shortfall
input_signals.hypothesis: Returns are lower when the gap between shareholder payouts and operating cash flow is large relative to external capital raised.
input_signals.reasoning: This directly measures how much of an external financing round is associated with payouts unsupported by internal cash generation. Unlike the prior matched-flow template, the ratio distinguishes firms whose financing primarily covers a payout shortfall from those whose operations already support distributions.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( dvc, prstkc ), oancf ), add( dltis, sstk ) ), 1 ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Funded Payout Deficit
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(ADD(dvc, prstkc), oancf), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term debt issuance predicts lower returns when shareholder payouts exceed operating cash flow.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal identifies firms adding fixed creditor claims while distributions to shareholders are unsupported by internal cash generation. Scaling both components by assets avoids the small external-financing denominator in the prior payout-shortfall ratio and tests debt-funded payout pressure directly.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( add( dvc, prstkc ), oancf ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Creditor-First Covered Payout
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(dvc, prstkc), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, dltr), ADD(dvc, prstkc)), ADD(ABS(SUB(oancf, dltr)), ADD(dvc, prstkc)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Meaningful shareholder payouts predict higher returns when operating cash flow covers both debt repayment and the distribution.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded residual applies a creditor-first financing hierarchy: cash must cover debt service before a payout is considered sustainable. Payout intensity prevents non-distributing firms from dominating the favorable portfolio, while the bounded form avoids small payout denominators.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( dvc, prstkc ), at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, dltr ), add( dvc, prstkc ) ), add( abs( sub( oancf, dltr ) ), add( dvc, prstkc ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Distressed Funding-Mix Instability
input_signals.hypothesis: Volatile switching between debt and equity financing predicts lower returns among firms with accumulated losses.
input_signals.reasoning: Volatility in the asset-scaled debt-minus-equity balance measures unstable funding-source access rather than the level of gross external financing. For deficit firms, repeated switching can reveal failed rescue rounds, market closure, or an inability to establish a durable capital structure.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( vol( ratio( sub( dltis, sstk ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( neg( ratio( re, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Creditor-First Covered Repurchase
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(prstkc, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(oancf, dltr), prstkc), ADD(ABS(SUB(oancf, dltr)), prstkc))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Share repurchases predict higher returns when operating cash flow covers debt repayment before funding the buyback.
input_signals.reasoning: Repurchases have favorable information content only when they do not compete with unsupported debt service. This controlled counterpart to the dividend signal tests whether the positive covered-payout effect is driven by flexible buybacks rather than recurring dividends.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( prstkc, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sub( oancf, dltr ), prstkc ), add( abs( sub( oancf, dltr ) ), prstkc ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt Issuance Under Service Shortfall
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(dltis, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltr, oancf), ADD(ABS(oancf), dltr))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Long-term debt issuance predicts lower returns when operating cash flow is insufficient relative to debt repayments.
input_signals.reasoning: The bounded shortfall term identifies genuinely uncovered debt service without dividing by a tiny repayment amount. New borrowing in that state is more likely to represent refinancing dependence than productive financing, aligning the issuance and distress channels in the negative direction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( dltis, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( dltr, oancf ), add( abs( oancf ), dltr ) ) ) )
